newsitem.title: USA: GPU submits Pennsylvania competition plan.
newsitem.headline: GPU submits Pennsylvania competition plan.

text.p: GPU Energy said Monday it filed with the Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission a proposed electric-competition pilot program.
Named PowerFuture, the program will enable about 51,000 Pennsylvania customers to pick their electricity supplier, the GPU Inc operating unit said.

"We hope to start implementing the program in April, subject to the PUC's approval of the program," said Dennis Baldassari, GPU Energy president. "Under the schedule we've outlined ... power deliveries are anticipated to begin in the fourth quarter of this year.
"The pilot will run until January 1, 1999, when the first phase-in of customer choice begins in Pennsylvania.

"Participating customers who choose to buy from an alternate electric supplier would receive a credit on their monthly electric bill," Baldassari said. "The credit would average about $0.0305 per kilowatt-hour.
Noting PowerFuture includes both energy and capacity, the company said it reflects both the cost of producing electricity and the cost of having generation available and ready to serve customers.

Five percent of GPU Energy's peak load in Pennsylvania -- about 194 megawatts -- will be available for the pilot competition program, it said. GPU's Metropolitan Edison subsidiary's customers will account for 98 megawatts and Pennsylvania Electric's for 96 megawatts.

An unregulated GPU affiliate is expected to participate in PowerFuture as a supplier, the company said. A code of conduct has been proposed to assure fairness in how GPU Energy and the affiliate interact.
GPU said customers eligible for PowerFuture will be picked in two groups.
The selection will be monitored by independent auditors and is expected to take place early in June.
These eligible customers will decide for themselves whether to participate in the program.

All of the some 25,000 residential and small commercial customers in eight randomly selected communities in the GPU Energy service area will be eligible to participate in the PowerFuture program, the company said.
In addition, about 26,000 randomly selected residential, commercial and industrial customers across the service territory will have the opportunity to test competition.
Of the about 51,000 total eligible for the pilot, an estimated 23,000 will be Met-Ed customers and 28,000 Penelec customers.

GPU said large industrial customers will be able to volunteer, but will be selected randomly if the available block of power is oversubscribed, it said, adding participation by commercial and industrial customers located in state certified Enterprise Zones is expected.

GPU will continue to deliver electricity to all customers and respond to power outages. It also will act as the backup supplier if deliveries aren't made or a supplier will no longer serve a customer, the company said.
There will be no charge to customers to participate in PowerFuture or to end their participation, although a customer who leaves the program won't be able to rejoin it.
